stage_2_story.text_en:
David had never stayed in a hotel abroad before, so when he arrived at his hotel in London, his eyes went wide. The lobby was enormous — marble floors, tall plants, and a grand chandelier overhead.

He approached the reception desk and gave his name. The agent found his reservation quickly and handed him a key card. David asked about the amenities, and the receptionist smiled: 'We have a gym, a restaurant, free Wi-Fi, and breakfast from seven to ten.' David nodded seriously, as though taking notes in a meeting.

That evening, after a long day of sightseeing, he was too tired to go out. He called room service and ordered a chicken sandwich and a pot of tea. It arrived in twenty minutes, warm and perfectly made. He ate in bed and felt like a king.

The next morning, he called housekeeping to ask for extra towels and to tidy the room. Then he went down to the lobby, where the concierge was waiting at his desk. David showed him a list of places he wanted to visit. The concierge smiled, made two phone calls, and handed David a full itinerary. 'Enjoy London,' he said.
